title: A 0.5pJ/bit 7.2Gbps HBM3 PHY on Intel4 with EMIB Packaging and Unmatched Receiver Architecture on PHY Side with Per Bit Deskew Correction
problem: High-bandwidth memory (HBM3) PHY design at advanced technology nodes faces challenges in power efficiency (pJ/bit), signal integrity across multi-die interconnects, and maintaining timing margins across temperature and process variations.
motivation: AI accelerators and data-center systems require high-capacity, low-latency memory with extreme energy efficiency. HBM3 at 7.2 Gbps per pin demands innovative receiver architectures and advanced I/O training to maintain reliability at energy budgets.
method: The design uses Intel 4 technology with EMIB packaging (connecting separate silicon components through embedded copper links) to build the memory PHY. It replaces standard transmitters with unterminated, low-swing versions (simpler senders that use less power by skipping termination resistors) and uses unmatched receiver paths (receivers that skip impedance-matching circuitry to save power). To maintain timing accuracy across temperature changes, it includes a linear voltage regulator (which removes electrical noise to reduce timing jitter), a per-bit deskew training algorithm (which adjusts the arrival time of each data line), and periodic sampling-point updates (which continuously check and shift when signals should be read).
key_novelty: The core idea is using simpler, unterminated transmitter and receiver designs combined with dynamic per-bit calibration and adaptive sampling-point updates to achieve both ultra-low power consumption and reliable high-speed operation.
contributions: 0.5 pJ/bit energy efficiency at 7.2 Gbps data rate (state-of-the-art power efficiency for HBM3)
Unterminated N-N low-swing transmitter design eliminating termination power
Unmatched receiver architecture reducing power overhead
Internal linear voltage regulator managing supply-induced deterministic jitter
Per-bit deskew (PBD) for per-pin eye optimization during advanced I/O training
Novel on-the-fly sampling-point update mitigating temperature-induced eye degradation without traffic interruption
limitations: Single technology node (Intel 4); portability to other nodes not discussed
No silicon measurement data or post-silicon validation results provided
Limited comparison with competing memory interface standards (DDR5, LPDDR5x)
On-the-fly calibration overhead and power consumption not quantified
EMIB packaging constraints and chiplet-to-chiplet latency not addressed
